title.en: Axisymmetric coil Green geometry and elliptic modulus

summary: From one axisymmetric observation point and multiple ring-coil centers, produce the GSEQ Green geometry: the source-regularized observation radius (r0 + 1e-8), each coil's squared elliptic modulus m = 4*r0*rl/((r0+rl)^2+(z0-zl)^2), and the Green distance denominator.

identity.relation: radius = observation_radius_m + 1e-8 (source axis-offset regularization); modulus_squared[l] = 4*radius*rl[l]/((radius+rl[l])^2+(z0-zl[l])^2); distance[l] = sqrt((radius+rl[l])^2+(z0-zl[l])^2).
identity.direction: observation point (R, Z) + ring-coil centers (rl, zl) -> regularized observation radius, per-coil squared moduli, per-coil distance denominators
identity.definition: The saved source's Green observation prologue: the axis offset r0 <- r0 + 1e-8 is an explicit contract of the original implementation (it regularizes the magnetic axis for Green evaluation) and must not be silently replaced by downstream special-function handling. The operator only generates the geometric quantities; it neither evaluates K, E nor the field responses.
identity.model: the saved formal implementation, ported verbatim
identity.geometry: one scalar observation point; ncoil ring coils in the same cylindrical frame
identity.boundary: finite inputs; positive coil radii; the regularized radius must remain finite and positive. A raw observation radius in (-1e-8, 0) is rejected (registered hardening: the offset would silently make it positive). A modulus of exactly 1 (observation point on a filament ring) is an admissible geometric output here; downstream Green-response consumers reject it as singular.
assumptions: Observation point and coil centers share one cylindrical frame.
The 1e-8 axis offset is the source's declared regularization, not a numerical repair.
No external physics reference is bound: the saved package records no validation_oracle_gap beyond the source anchoring.

inputs.name: observation_radius_m
inputs.description: Raw cylindrical radius of the observation point.
inputs.constraints: Finite; must be nonnegative (a raw radius in (-1e-8, 0) is rejected: the source offset would silently regularize it to a positive one -- registered hardening); the regularized radius must be finite and positive.

inputs.name: observation_z_m
inputs.description: Axial coordinate of the observation point.

inputs.name: coil_radius_m
inputs.constraints: Finite 1-D with strictly positive entries, same shape as coil_z_m.

outputs.name: regularized_radius_m
outputs.description: Observation radius after the source axis offset, the value downstream GSEQ Green operators must receive.
outputs.constraints: Finite and positive; paired once with the response operator (which does not offset again).

outputs.name: modulus_squared
outputs.description: Per-coil squared elliptic modulus m = k^2.
outputs.constraints: Finite values in (0, 1] on accepted non-singular geometry; overflow from finite but extreme inputs raises ValueError (registered hardening); exactly 1 marks an observation point on the filament ring (singular downstream).

outputs.name: distance_m
outputs.description: Per-coil Green geometric distance denominator sqrt((r0+rl)^2+(z0-zl)^2).

preconditions: Observation point and coil centres are given in one cylindrical frame with SI metre coordinates.
supported: GSEQ Green geometry generation (regularized radius, per-coil squared modulus, distance denominator) for filament-coil Green evaluation.
excluded: Complete elliptic integral evaluation, the Green field responses, arbitrary-point (non-scalar) target sets, and the baseline scipy-elliptic filament relation.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError when any coordinate is non-finite, when coil radii are non-positive or misaligned, or when the regularized radius is non-positive.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if the modulus or distance overflow to non-finite values for finite but extreme input magnitudes (registered hardening); no partial results are returned.

provenance.lineage_summary: Development integration from the saved GSEQ 轴对称线圈几何模数 package (gseq operators bundle), source anchor GSEQ filament-coil Green observation prologue, as recorded by the saved bundle's own provenance section. Arithmetic ported verbatim; the port adds a registered input hardening: a raw observation radius in (-1e-8, 0) is rejected instead of being silently regularized to a positive one by the axis offset. The saved GSEQ bundle supports bounded historical development comparison; qualified-L1 delivery root remains empty, so this is not qualified-L1 provenance and not expert approval.
source_kinds: saved L1 operator document and implementation

example.description: Generate the GSEQ Green geometry for one observation point and two coils; the regularized radius carries the source axis offset.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import compute_axisymmetric_coil_modulus
radius, modulus, distance = compute_axisymmetric_coil_modulus(
    0.3, 0.0, np.array([0.2, 0.2]), np.array([-0.1, 0.1]))
assert radius == 0.3 + 1e-8
assert np.all((modulus > 0.0) & (modulus <= 1.0))
assert np.all(distance > 0.0)
example.expected: The regularized radius equals 0.3 + 1e-8; moduli lie in (0, 1]; distances are positive.

scope: Source-regularized geometry quantities against an independent recomputation.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The maintained direct tests establish the regularized radius, per-coil moduli and distance denominators against an independent recomputation (exact float equality on the offset, rtol=1e-15 on the closed forms), the (0, 1] modulus range on admissible geometry, axis-point admissibility through the source offset, and the fail-closed input contracts. No test establishes the geometry against an external physics reference; the relation is a direct closed-form contract of the saved source.
known_limitations: The saved GSEQ bundle supports bounded historical development comparison only; qualified-L1 delivery root is empty.
Registered input hardening: raw observation radii in (-1e-8, 0) are rejected rather than silently regularized to positive values by the source axis offset.

Registered output hardening: finite but extreme input magnitudes (e.g. r0 = rl = 1e308) that overflow the squared geometry sums are rejected with ValueError instead of handing non-finite modulus/distance downstream (the saved implementation returns them silently).
A modulus of exactly 1 (observation point on a filament ring) is an admissible output; consumers must reject it (the response operator does).
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.
